title: Group Continuous Dates
learning_objective: Learn how date minus row_number groups consecutive dates.

tutorial.explanation: Like the id - row_number trick, date - row_number stays constant for continuous dates inside each status.
tutorial.syntax: CAST(status_date AS DATE) - CAST(ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY period_state ORDER BY status_date) AS INTEGER)
tutorial.mental_model: If dates increase one day at a time and row numbers increase one at a time, subtracting row number creates a stable group key.

guided_example.prompt: Find start and end date for each continuous status interval.
guided_example.solution_query: WITH numbered AS (SELECT period_state, status_date, CAST(status_date AS DATE) - CAST(ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY period_state ORDER BY status_date) AS INTEGER) AS group_key FROM timeline) SELECT period_state, MIN(status_date) AS start_date, MAX(status_date) AS end_date FROM numbered GROUP BY period_state, group_key;
guided_example.explanation: The group key stays constant inside continuous dates for the same period_state.

practice.prompt: Return period_state, start_date, and end_date for continuous date groups.
practice.expected_query: WITH numbered AS (SELECT period_state, status_date, CAST(status_date AS DATE) - CAST(ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY period_state ORDER BY status_date) AS INTEGER) AS group_key FROM timeline) SELECT period_state, MIN(status_date) AS start_date, MAX(status_date) AS end_date FROM numbered GROUP BY period_state, group_key;

hints: Group by period_state and the computed key.
